learn: A line is a mark that goes from one point to another.
Artists use lines to draw shapes, show edges and make patterns.
You can make a line with a pencil, a crayon, a brush or even a stick in the sand.
check: A mark from one point to another
What can you make a line with?
lessons.try: Draw five lines with a crayon, each one different.

learn: Lines can be straight or curvy.
Lines can be zigzag, wavy, dotted or spiral.
Lines can be thick or thin.
check: Which line looks like a snake?
Which line goes up and down in sharp points?
A line can be thick or...
lessons.try: Draw a straight line, a wavy line, a zigzag line and a spiral.

learn: Lines can show how things feel or move.
Soft wavy lines can look calm, like water.
Sharp zigzag lines can look exciting, like lightning.
check: Which line can look like lightning?
lessons.try: Draw a calm picture with wavy lines and an exciting picture with zigzag lines.

learn: When a line closes up, it makes a shape.
Circles, squares, triangles and rectangles are basic shapes.
Shapes can be big or small.
check: What does a closed line make?
How many sides does a triangle have?
lessons.try: Draw a circle, a square, a triangle and a rectangle.

learn: Artists put shapes together to make pictures.
A house can be a square with a triangle roof.
A snowman can be three circles.
check: What shape could be a roof?
A snowman can be made of...
Can shapes be put together to make pictures?
lessons.try: Make a robot using only shapes.

learn: Some shapes are free-form, like leaves, clouds and puddles.
These are called organic shapes.
Look around: you can find both kinds of shapes everywhere.
lessons.try: Trace the shape of a leaf and colour it in.

learn: The primary colours are red, yellow and blue.
They are special because you cannot make them by mixing other colours.
Many other colours come from them.
check: How many primary colours are there?
Can you mix other colours to make a primary colour?
lessons.try: Paint three dots: one red, one yellow and one blue.

learn: Red can be a fire truck or a strawberry.
Yellow can be the sun or a banana.
Blue can be the sky or the sea.
check: What colour is the clear sky?
lessons.try: Find one red, one yellow and one blue thing in your home.

learn: Use a clean brush for each colour so the colours stay bright.
Rinse your brush in water between colours.
Dab off extra water on a paper towel.
check: What do you dab extra water on?
Which colours did you use for this painting?
lessons.try: Paint a picture using only red, yellow and blue.

learn: When you mix two primary colours you make a secondary colour.
Red and yellow make orange. Yellow and blue make green. Red and blue make purple.
Orange, green and purple are the secondary colours.
lessons.try: Mix yellow and blue paint and see what colour you get.

learn: Adding white makes a colour lighter. Light red is pink.
Adding a little black makes a colour darker.
Artists use light and dark to make pictures interesting.
check: What do you add to make a colour lighter?
lessons.try: Make three blues: light, normal and dark.

learn: A colour wheel shows colours in a circle.
Each secondary colour sits between the two primary colours that make it.
Orange sits between red and yellow.
check: What does a colour wheel show?
lessons.try: Make a colour wheel with six colours.

learn: Texture is how something feels when you touch it.
Things can be rough, smooth, soft, bumpy or fuzzy.
A rock may be rough. A mirror is smooth. A kitten is soft.
lessons.try: Touch five things and say how each one feels.

learn: Artists can draw texture so you can almost feel it with your eyes.
Short lines can look like fur. Dots can look like sand.
Swirls can look like curly hair.
check: What can short lines look like?
lessons.try: Draw a furry animal using short lines.

learn: A rubbing copies texture onto paper.
Put paper over something bumpy, like a leaf or a coin, and rub with the side of a crayon.
The texture appears like magic.
check: What part of the crayon do you rub with?
What could you make a rubbing of?
lessons.try: Make a rubbing of a leaf.

learn: A pattern is something that repeats.
Red, blue, red, blue is a pattern.
Patterns can use colours, shapes or lines.
check: What comes next: red, blue, red, blue, ...?
lessons.try: Make a pattern with two colours of crayons.

learn: Patterns are everywhere.
Zebras have stripes. Brick walls have rows of bricks. Some shirts have checks or dots.
Look for patterns on your clothes, floors and walls.
check: What pattern does a zebra have?
What repeats on a brick wall?
lessons.try: Find three patterns in your house.

learn: You can make a pattern border around a picture.
Try shape patterns like circle, triangle, circle, triangle.
Try harder patterns with three things: star, heart, moon, star, heart, moon.
check: What comes next: circle, triangle, circle, ...?
What comes next: star, heart, moon, star, heart, ...?
Where can a pattern go in a picture?
Around the edge as a border
lessons.try: Draw a pattern border around a drawing of yourself.

learn: A self-portrait is a picture of yourself.
Look in a mirror. What shape is your face? What colour are your eyes and hair?
Artists look carefully before they draw.
check: What can help you see your face?
lessons.try: Look in a mirror for one minute. Say what you see.

learn: Start with an oval for the face.
Eyes go about halfway down. The nose goes below the eyes and the mouth below the nose.
Ears are at the sides, about as high as the eyes.
check: What shape is good to start a face?
lessons.try: Draw your face with all the parts.

learn: Add things that show who you are, like your favourite colours or a pet.
Your face can show feelings: happy, surprised or calm.
Every self-portrait is different, because every person is different.
check: How can a self-portrait show who you are?
lessons.try: Add your favourite thing to your self-portrait.

learn: A collage is art made by gluing pieces onto paper.
You can use paper scraps, fabric, leaves, buttons or magazine pictures.
The word collage comes from a French word that means to glue.
check: What could go in a collage?
Collage comes from a word meaning...
lessons.try: Collect five scraps you could use in a collage.

learn: You can tear paper for soft edges or cut it for sharp edges.
Hold scissors safely, pointing away from you, and only use them for paper.
Put scraps in a tray so you can find them.
check: How do you hold scissors safely?
lessons.try: Tear one piece of paper and cut another. Compare the edges.

learn: Plan first. Move the pieces around before you glue.
Use a little glue, not a lot.
Big pieces go down first, small details on top.
check: What do you do before gluing?
lessons.try: Make a collage of a garden.

learn: A sculpture is art you can walk around and see from all sides.
Paintings are flat. Sculptures have height, width and depth.
Sculptures can be made of clay, wood, stone or even paper.
check: Art you can see from all sides
What can sculptures be made of?
lessons.try: Find a sculpture in a picture or a park.

learn: You can roll clay into a ball or a snake.
You can pinch it, press it and pull it into shapes.
A pinch pot is made by pressing your thumb into a ball of clay and pinching the sides.
check: How do you start a pinch pot?
Press your thumb into a ball
What can you roll clay into?
lessons.try: Make a pinch pot from clay or play dough.

learn: Paper can stand up too. Fold it, curl it or roll it into tubes.
Tape tubes together to make a tower.
Paper sculptures can be animals, buildings or anything you imagine.
check: What can you make with paper tubes?
lessons.try: Build a paper tower that stands by itself.

learn: When we look at art, we take our time.
We ask: What do I see? What colours, lines and shapes are there?
There are no wrong answers when you say what you see.
check: How should we look at art?
Are there wrong answers when you say what you see?
lessons.try: Look at a painting for one minute and name three things you see.

learn: We can say how a picture makes us feel.
We listen when friends share. People may feel different things.
We use kind words about everyone's art.
check: What can we say about art?
Do people feel the same about all art?
No, they may feel different things
What words do we use about art?
lessons.try: Tell a friend how a picture makes you feel.

learn: An art show is a place to share art.
Each artist picks a favourite piece and gives it a title.
Visitors walk quietly and look at each piece.
check: What does each artist give their art?
How do visitors walk at an art show?
lessons.try: Pick your favourite art from this year and give it a title.
